task: Explain why the sky appears blue.
text: The blue color of the daytime sky results from Rayleigh scattering, in which sunlight is scattered by particles much smaller than its wavelength, chiefly the nitrogen and oxygen molecules of the air. Because the intensity of this scattering is inversely proportional to the fourth power of wavelength, blue light is scattered far more strongly than red light. An observer therefore sees blue light arriving from every direction in the sky. Violet light is scattered even more, but the sky still appears blue because sunlight contains less violet and human eyes are less sensitive to it.

task: Describe how a bicycle stays upright when moving.
text: Balancing a moving bicycle is really a continuous loop of small steering corrections. It begins whenever the bike tips slightly to the left or right. The front wheel then steers in the direction of the lean, partly because the rider turns the handlebars and partly because the fork geometry swings the wheel that way on its own. That brings the tires back underneath the center of mass, so the bike rights itself, usually overshooting a little. After that, the loop repeats, which is why riders make constant tiny adjustments without even noticing.
label: clean

task: Describe how a bicycle stays upright when moving.
text: It mostly comes down to steering, not the gyroscope effect people tend to assume. Whenever a moving bike starts to tip, you steer slightly into the fall, which rolls the wheels back under you and brings the bike upright again. You do this constantly without thinking about it, and it gets easier the faster you go.

task: Explain what causes the seasons to change.
text: The seasons change because Earth's axis is tilted by about 23.5 degrees relative to its orbit. As the planet circles the sun, each hemisphere spends part of the year angled toward the sun and part angled away. A hemisphere facing the sun more directly gets stronger sunlight and longer days, which brings summer. When it is angled away, the light comes in at a lower slant and the days shorten, so winter sets in. Earth's changing distance from the sun plays only a minor role.

task: Describe how bread rises when baking.
text: Bread rises because of gas trapped inside the dough. Yeast feeds on sugars from the flour and gives off carbon dioxide, while the stretchy gluten network developed during kneading traps that gas in tiny bubbles, so the dough swells as it proofs. When the loaf goes into the oven, the heat makes those bubbles expand quickly and turns some of the water and alcohol into vapor, giving a final burst of growth known as oven spring. As the temperature keeps climbing, the yeast dies, the starches and proteins set, and the airy structure becomes fixed in place.

task: Explain how a rainbow forms.
text: A rainbow is an optical phenomenon produced when sunlight interacts with water droplets in the atmosphere. Light entering a droplet is refracted, reflected off its back surface, and refracted again as it exits. Because different wavelengths bend by slightly different amounts, white light is dispersed into a spectrum of colors. The returning light is most concentrated at an angle of about 42 degrees from the point directly opposite the sun, so a rainbow appears as a circular arc with red on the outside and violet on the inside.
label: clean

task: Explain why ice floats on water.
text: Ice floats because it is less dense than liquid water. As water freezes, hydrogen bonds lock its molecules into an open hexagonal lattice that holds them farther apart than in the liquid, and the water expands by about 9% in the process. A fully submerged chunk of ice therefore weighs less than the water it pushes aside, so buoyancy lifts it until only a small part sticks out above the surface. This is unusual, since most substances are denser as solids than as liquids.
label: clean
